name: What costs are usually missing from custom home quotes?

mainEntity.name: What hidden or commonly omitted costs should I watch for in a custom home construction estimate?
mainEntity.text: What hidden or commonly omitted costs should I watch for in a custom home construction estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many custom home estimates look complete at first glance but leave out major items that appear later as change orders. Common omissions include design and engineering, permit and plan check fees, surveys, geotechnical reports, utility upgrades, trenching beyond the base scope, landscaping, site fencing, temporary power and water, and high-end finish allowances. In luxury projects, another frequent gap is the difference between an allowance and the real cost of the selected fixture or material. Homeowners should also check whether the quote includes demolition, haul-away, protection of neighboring property, appliance installation, and final cleaning. The safest approach is to ask for an inclusions schedule that defines exactly what is and is not covered. That makes it easier to compare contractors fairly and helps reduce disputes once construction starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Custom home quotes often miss soft costs, utility upgrades, permit fees, soil and survey work, landscape scope, appliance allowances, specialty finishes, and changes required by plan check. Some bids also leave out temporary utilities, site protection, or final punch-list items. Owners should compare bids line by line, not just by total price.
